title: Runway-based memory budgeting for continuous inference
creator: Ava Chen
description:
Problem: Continuous batching plus large KV caches creates volatile GPU memory pressure across weights, KV and activations. Current headroom heuristics are reactive and either over-reserve (higher costs) or under-reserve (OOM risk) for mixed-priority multi-tenant workloads.

Goal: Design and implement a lightweight "memory runway" system that computes a short-term sustainable memory budget per-GPU and per-tenant. The runway score expresses how long current allocations are expected to remain safe under recent request patterns (tokens/s, average seq lengths, KV hit ratio). Use the runway to drive dynamic soft-reservations: graceful activation spooling, KV eviction aggressiveness, and per-tenant micro-burst allowances.

Approach (high-level):
- Runtime telemetry: extend the memory telemetry stream with sliding-window token throughput, median seq length, KV-add/evict rates, and measured eviction latency.
- Runway model: an exponential-weighted predictor that estimates how much memory delta will be consumed over the next T seconds for weights/KV/activations separately, then computes "runway_seconds" = safe_headroom / predicted_consumption_rate.
- Policy tiers: map runway_seconds to a soft policy ladder (green/yellow/red) that controls: batch admission rate, proactive KV trimming, activation spill thresholds, and whether to accept burst requests.
- Per-tenant and global pooling: calculate both per-tenant runway and a global GPU runway to allow short-lived cross-tenant bursting if global runway permits, while preventing cascading evictions.
- Simulation & SLOs: run stochastic request trace simulations (from production traces) to choose thresholds that meet 99.9% no-OOM SLO with minimal cost uplift.

Deliverables: design doc, runtime telemetry schema change, runway predictor component, policy engine (configurable), tests + simulation harness, Console dashboard tiles (runway per-GPU, per-tenant), rollout plan with canary and rollback criteria.
comments: 2026-02-19 - Kickoff: synced with infra and runtime teams. Agreed runway should be a runtime-side heuristic exposed to control-plane. Action: Diego to draft design doc, Priya to provide representative traces.

2026-02-24 - Design draft completed (confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/Runway+Memory+Budgeting). Reduced scope to avoid kernel-level changes in V1. Focus: telemetry + policy layer + conservative predictor.

2026-03-02 - Runtime telemetry prototype in branch feat/runway-telemetry. Added sliding-window token rate and KV delta counters. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving/pull/1386 (WIP). Front-end: design requested runway visual mockups from design (DES-...).

2026-03-05 - Simulation results: using a 30s prediction window and EWMA alpha=0.3 produced stable runway_seconds distribution; median runway for noisy tenants ~45s. Noted edge-case: long tails from streaming sessions cause runway oscillation; proposal to add session-aware smoothing.

2026-03-08 - Review feedback from SRE & Product: SRE wants hard backstop to always prefer eviction over failing requests; Product wants configurable degradation ladder to preserve latency-sensitive routes. Action: add policy config knobs and a hard-oom-backstop flag.
- SRE comment: https://github.com/redwood-inference/ops-plays/pull/92#discussion_r12345

2026-03-10 - Implementation: basic runway predictor merged into staging telemetry (PR #1386 merged). Policy engine landed behind feature flag runway-experiment. Running staged canary on two dedicates for 48h. Next: add acceptance tests and console tiles.
2026-03-10 - Diego: Assign follow-ups for metrics instrumentation (ENG-540008) and simulation harness improvements (ENG-540009).
acceptance_criteria: Runtime exposes "runway_seconds" metric per-GPU and per-tenant in telemetry stream (prometheus/OTel).

Policy engine consumes runway metric and enacts soft-reservations: at yellow ladder reduce batch admission by configurable fraction; at red ladder proactively trim KV by configurable percentage before denying requests.
No increase in OOM incidents during 48h canary on dedicated hosts compared to baseline (target: <= baseline + 1%).
Simulation harness demonstrates chosen thresholds meet 99.9% no-OOM target across three historical trace buckets (steady, bursty, streaming).
Console shows runway tiles (per-GPU and per-tenant) and an incident drill-down linking runway drops to eviction activity.
Feature guarded by runway-experiment feature flag and rollout plan documented (canary -> phased -> rollback criteria defined).
notes: Tradeoffs: Conservative runway thresholds reduce throughput and increase cost. We aim to choose thresholds that primarily throttle best-effort routes while preserving latency SLOs for high-priority routes.

Open questions: 1) How to incorporate KV hit-rate into predicted consumption more accurately for large streaming sessions; 2) Where to store per-tenant burst credits to persist across short reconnects.

Related artifacts: design doc (Confluence): https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/Runway+Memory+Budgeting, simulation notebook: gs://redwood-data/sim/runway-sims-2026-02-28.ipynb, PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving/pull/1386
Risk & mitigation: Risk of policy oscillation for tail-heavy tenants. Mitigation: session-aware smoothing + minimum policy hold time of 10s to avoid flip-flopping.
